section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of change versus accumulation using a Cheetah. A Cheetah's speedometer shows its 'Derivative' (velocity at an instant), while the total distance it covers represents the 'Integral' (accumulation over time). The goal is to show these aren't separate math topics, but two sides of the same coin.
section_1.example: Visual: A Cheetah running across a savannah. An overlay shows a graph where the x-axis is time and the y-axis is speed. As the cheetah speeds up, the point on the graph moves higher.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: The Slope of Change
section_2.content: Briefly review the Derivative as the rate of change. Visually represent this as the slope of a tangent line on a position-time graph. Remind students that if we have Position, the Derivative gives us Velocity.
section_2.example: Visual: A curve representing a hiker climbing a hill. A zooming lens shows a 'magnified' straight line (the tangent) at a specific point, highlighting the steepness.

section_3.title: The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards
section_3.content: Introduce the idea of 'Anti-differentiation.' If we have the velocity (the derivative), how do we find the total distance (the original function)? This sets the stage for the Integral as the 'undoing' of the Derivative.
section_3.example: Visual: A 'Function Machine' where you drop in a function like x². The 'Derivative Lever' turns it into 2x. To get back to x², we need the 'Integral Lever'.

section_4.title: Visualizing Accumulation: The Area Under the Curve
section_4.content: Define the Integral graphically as the area between the function's curve and the x-axis. Explain that just as a derivative looks at a single 'point' of change, an integral looks at the 'sum' of all changes over an interval.
section_4.example: Visual: A robot arm painting the area under a curve. As the arm moves from left to right, the colored area grows, representing the accumulated value.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
section_5.content: Present the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC). Explain that the area under a rate curve (f) can be found using its anti-derivative (F). This is the 'Aha!' moment where the slope and the area are mathematically linked.
section_5.example: Mathematical Formula: ∫[a,b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Visual: Two screens side-by-side. Screen A shows the area filling up; Screen B shows a point moving up a position graph. They move in perfect synchronization.

section_6.title: Example Walkthrough: The Leaky Tank
section_6.content: Apply the concept to a physics problem. A tank is leaking water at a rate defined by a function. We use the integral to find exactly how much total water was lost over 10 minutes.
section_6.example: Character: 'Rusty the Robot' is watching a water tank. The rate of flow is v(t) = 2t. By integrating, we find the volume V(t) = t², showing that after 10 minutes, 100 liters have leaked.

section_7.title: Summary: The Calculus Loop
section_7.content: Reinforce the 'Circular' nature of the relationship. Differentiation takes you from Accumulation to Rate; Integration takes you from Rate to Accumulation. End with a high-level visual summary.
section_7.example: Visual: An infinity-symbol shaped track. One side is labeled 'Derivatives (Rates)' and the other 'Integrals (Totals)'. A spark travels around the loop, connecting the two concepts forever.

section_3.example: Visual: A 'Function Machine' where you drop in a function like x². The 'Derivative Lever' turns it into 2x. To get back to x², we need the 'Integral Lever'.

section_4.title: Visualizing Accumulation: The Area Under the Curve
section_4.content: Define the Integral graphically as the area between the function's curve and the x-axis. Explain that just as a derivative looks at a single 'point' of change, an integral looks at the 'sum' of all changes over an interval.
section_4.example: Visual: A robot arm painting the area under a curve. As the arm moves from left to right, the colored area grows, representing the accumulated value.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
section_5.content: Present the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC). Explain that the area under a rate curve (f) can be found using its anti-derivative (F). This is the 'Aha!' moment where the slope and the area are mathematically linked.
section_5.example: Mathematical Formula: ∫[a,b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Visual: Two screens side-by-side. Screen A shows the area filling up; Screen B shows a point moving up a position graph. They move in perfect synchronization.

section_6.title: Example Walkthrough: The Leaky Tank
section_6.content: Apply the concept to a physics problem. A tank is leaking water at a rate defined by a function. We use the integral to find exactly how much total water was lost over 10 minutes.
section_6.example: Character: 'Rusty the Robot' is watching a water tank. The rate of flow is v(t) = 2t. By integrating, we find the volume V(t) = t², showing that after 10 minutes, 100 liters have leaked.

section_7.title: Summary: The Calculus Loop
section_7.content: Reinforce the 'Circular' nature of the relationship. Differentiation takes you from Accumulation to Rate; Integration takes you from Rate to Accumulation. End with a high-level visual summary.
section_7.example: Visual: An infinity-symbol shaped track. One side is labeled 'Derivatives (Rates)' and the other 'Integrals (Totals)'. A spark travels around the loop, connecting the two concepts forever.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed.
The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change.
This specific value is known as the derivative.
The total distance covered represents the accumulated change.
In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral.
animations: A cheetah appears on the left and starts running across the screen.
A velocity-time graph appears above the cheetah with axes labeled in #FFFFFF.
A point moves along the graph's curve as the cheetah's speed varies.
The y-axis value is highlighted in #00FF00 and labeled 'Derivative (Speed)'.
The area under the curve is shaded in #FFFF00 and labeled 'Integral (Distance)'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: The Slope of Change
lecture_lines: Differentiation helps us calculate the rate of change.
Graphically, the derivative is the slope of the tangent.
It transforms a position function into a velocity function.
animations: A position-time curve for a hiker appears in #ADD8E6.
A zooming lens highlights a point on the curve, revealing a tangent line.
The tangent line's slope is colored #FFA500 and labeled 'Velocity (Derivative)'.

section_3.title: The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards
lecture_lines: Integration is the inverse process of finding the derivative.
If we have velocity, we can recover total distance.
We call this process anti-differentiation or finding the integral.
animations: A 'Function Machine' illustration appears in the center in #C0C0C0.
The function x^2 enters, a lever labeled 'Derivative' is pulled, and 2x exits.
The function 2x enters, a lever labeled 'Integral' is pulled, and x^2 exits.

section_4.title: Visualizing Accumulation: The Area Under the Curve
lecture_lines: Visually, the integral represents the area under a curve.
It sums up infinite tiny changes over an interval.
This total area equals the accumulated value of change.
animations: A continuous function curve f(x) is drawn in #FF69B4.
A vertical line moves from x=a to x=b, shading the area below the curve.
The shaded area is labeled 'Integral' in #FFFF00 to represent accumulation.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
lecture_lines: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus bridges slope and area.
It connects the derivative of a function to its integral.
The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.
Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.
This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus.
animations: The FTC formula \int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a) appears in #FFFFFF.
The screen splits into two panels: Panel A (left) and Panel B (right).

Panel B shows a point on the graph of F(x) rising in #00BFFF.
A bridge icon in #FFD700 connects the panels as they animate in sync.

section_6.title: Example Walkthrough: The Leaky Tank
lecture_lines: Consider a tank leaking water at a changing rate.
Integrating the flow rate gives the total volume lost.
Calculus provides exact answers for these real-world problems.
animations: A leaky water tank appears with water level decreasing over time.
The rate function v(t) = 2t is plotted on a graph in #FF4500.
The integral calculation [t^2] from 0 to 10 appears, resulting in 100 liters.

section_7.title: Summary: The Calculus Loop
lecture_lines: Derivatives and integrals form a beautiful, continuous cycle.
Differentiation breaks a whole down into its parts.
Integration builds those parts back into a whole.
They are two sides of the same mathematical coin.
Master this connection to unlock the power of calculus.

The right loop is labeled 'Integrals (Totals)' in #FFFF00.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.place_at_grid(velocity_label, "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(velocity_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for final state
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.4)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.1 # Adjusted for 6 columns on right
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9 # Adjusted for 6 rows
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Example Walkthrough: The Leaky Tank",
            [
                "Consider a tank leaking water at a changing rate.",
                "Integrating the flow rate gives the total volume lost.",
                "Calculus provides exact answers for these real-world problems."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_TANK = "#808080"
        COLOR_WATER = "#1E90FF"
        COLOR_FLOW = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_MATH = "#00FF7F"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Tank Setup
        tank_frame = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2.0, color=COLOR_TANK, stroke_width=4)
        water_level = ValueTracker(1.8) # Initial height
        
        # Water inside the tank
        water = always_redraw(lambda: Rectangle(
            width=2.45, 
            height=water_level.get_value(),
            fill_color=COLOR_WATER,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=0
        ).align_to(tank_frame, BOTTOM).shift(UP * 0.025))
        
        # Leak droplet
        leak_point = tank_frame.get_bottom() + DOWN * 0.1
        droplet = Dot(point=leak_point, color=COLOR_WATER, radius=0.08)
        
        tank_group = VGroup(tank_frame, water)
        self.place_in_area(tank_group, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(tank_frame), FadeIn(water))
        
        # Leaking animation
        def animate_leak():
            self.play(
                water_level.animate.set_value(1.0),
                Succession(
                    *[
                        Succession(
                            droplet.animate.move_to(leak_point + DOWN * 1.5).set_opacity(0),
                            droplet.animate.move_to(leak_point).set_opacity(1),
                            run_time=0.5
                        ) for _ in range(3)
                    ]
                ),
                run_time=3,
                rate_func=linear
            )

        self.add(droplet)
        animate_leak()
        self.remove(droplet)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Graph for v(t) = 2t
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 11, 2],
            y_range=[0, 22, 5],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 24},
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="v(t)")
        graph = axes.plot(lambda t: 2*t, x_range=[0, 10], color=COLOR_FLOW)
        graph_label = MathTex("v(t) = 2t", color=COLOR_FLOW, font_size=24).next_to(graph, UP)
        
        # Shaded area for integral
        area = axes.get_area(graph, x_range=[0, 10], color=COLOR_FLOW, opacity=0.3)
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, labels, graph, graph_label, area)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(labels))
        self.play(Create(graph), Write(graph_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Integral calculation
        calc = MathTex(
            r"V = \int_{0}^{10} 2t \, dt = [t^2]_{0}^{10} = 100 \text{ liters}",
            color=COLOR_MATH,
            font_size=32
        )
        
        self.place_in_area(calc, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset colors
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

            "This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus."

        label_b.next_to(ax_b, UP, buff=0.1)

            ax_a.c2p(0, 0),
            *[ax_a.c2p(x, 2*x) for x in np.linspace(0, tracker.get_value(), 20)],
            ax_a.c2p(tracker.get_value(), 0),
            ax_a.c2p(0, 0)
        ]))

        # Point on F(x) - persistent mobject
        dot_b = Dot(color="#00BFFF")
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ax_b.c2p(tracker.get_value(), tracker.get_value()**2)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.
        # Panel A shows area under f(x) filling up in #00FF00.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.add(area)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.
        # Panel B shows a point on the graph of F(x) rising in #00BFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.add(dot_b)
        self.play(Indicate(dot_b), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus.
        # A bridge icon in #FFD700 connects the panels as they animate in sync.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        bridge = DoubleArrow(
            start=ax_a.get_right(), 
            end=ax_b.get_left(), 
            color="#FFD700", 
            buff=0.1, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        bridge_label = Text("FTC BRIDGE", font_size=14, color="#FFD700").next_to(bridge, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        self.play(Create(bridge), Write(bridge_label))
        
        # Final sync movement
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus bridges slope and area.",
            "It connects the derivative of a function to its integral.",
            "The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.",
            "Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.",
            "This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Dim all lecture lines initially
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_color(GRAY)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus bridges slope and area.
        # FTC formula \int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a) appears in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        formula = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # It connects the derivative of a function to its integral.
        # The screen splits into two panels: Panel A (left) and Panel B (right).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Panel A: f(x) = 2x
        ax_a = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 6], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5, 
                   axis_config={"include_tip": False}).set_color(GRAY)
        label_a = Text("Rate: f(x)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        panel_a = VGroup(ax_a, label_a)
        label_a.next_to(ax_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(panel_a, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Panel B: F(x) = x^2
        ax_b = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 9], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5,
                   axis_config={"include_tip": False}).set_color(GRAY)
        label_b = Text("Accumulation: F(x)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        panel_b = VGroup(ax_b, label_b)
        label_b.next_to(ax_b, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(panel_b, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(ax_a), Create(label_a), Create(ax_b), Create(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # Prepare for sync animations
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        
        f_curve = ax_a.plot(lambda x: 2*x, x_range=[0, 2.5], color=WHITE)
        F_curve = ax_b.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.5], color=WHITE)
        self.add(f_curve, F_curve)

        # Area under f(x) - persistent mobject
        area = VMobject(color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0)
        area.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners([
            ax_a.c2p(0, 0),
            *[ax_a.c2p(x, 2*x) for x in np.linspace(0, tracker.get_value(), 20)],
            ax_a.c2p(tracker.get_value(), 0),
            ax_a.c2p(0, 0)
        ]))

        # Point on F(x) - persistent mobject
        dot_b = Dot(color="#00BFFF")
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ax_b.c2p(tracker.get_value(), tracker.get_value()**2)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.
        # Panel A shows area under f(x) filling up in #00FF00.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.add(area)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.
        # Panel B shows a point on the graph of F(x) rising in #00BFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.add(dot_b)
        self.play(Indicate(dot_b), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus.
        # A bridge icon in #FFD700 connects the panels as they animate in sync.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        bridge = DoubleArrow(
            start=ax_a.get_right(), 
            end=ax_b.get_left(), 
            color="#FFD700", 
            buff=0.1, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        bridge_label = Text("FTC BRIDGE", font_size=14, color="#FFD700").next_to(bridge, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        self.play(Create(bridge), Write(bridge_label))
        
        # Final sync movement
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard

        lecture_lines = [
            "Visually, the integral represents the area under a curve.",
            "It sums up infinite tiny changes over an interval.",
            "This total area equals the accumulated value of change."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FF69B4"
        LABEL_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        )

            curve, 
            x_range=[0.5, x_tracker.get_value()], 
            color=SHADE_COLOR, 
            opacity=0.3
        ))

section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of change versus accumulation using a Cheetah. A Cheetah's speedometer shows its 'Derivative' (velocity at an instant), while the total distance it covers represents the 'Integral' (accumulation over time). The goal is to show these aren't separate math topics, but two sides of the same coin.
section_1.example: Visual: A Cheetah running across a savannah. An overlay shows a graph where the x-axis is time and the y-axis is speed. As the cheetah speeds up, the point on the graph moves higher.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: The Slope of Change
section_2.content: Briefly review the Derivative as the rate of change. Visually represent this as the slope of a tangent line on a position-time graph. Remind students that if we have Position, the Derivative gives us Velocity.
section_2.example: Visual: A curve representing a hiker climbing a hill. A zooming lens shows a 'magnified' straight line (the tangent) at a specific point, highlighting the steepness.

section_3.title: The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards
section_3.content: Introduce the idea of 'Anti-differentiation.' If we have the velocity (the derivative), how do we find the total distance (the original function)? This sets the stage for the Integral as the 'undoing' of the Derivative.
section_3.example: Visual: A 'Function Machine' where you drop in a function like x². The 'Derivative Lever' turns it into 2x. To get back to x², we need the 'Integral Lever'.

section_4.title: Visualizing Accumulation: The Area Under the Curve
section_4.content: Define the Integral graphically as the area between the function's curve and the x-axis. Explain that just as a derivative looks at a single 'point' of change, an integral looks at the 'sum' of all changes over an interval.
section_4.example: Visual: A robot arm painting the area under a curve. As the arm moves from left to right, the colored area grows, representing the accumulated value.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
section_5.content: Present the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC). Explain that the area under a rate curve (f) can be found using its anti-derivative (F). This is the 'Aha!' moment where the slope and the area are mathematically linked.
section_5.example: Mathematical Formula: ∫[a,b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Visual: Two screens side-by-side. Screen A shows the area filling up; Screen B shows a point moving up a position graph. They move in perfect synchronization.

section_6.title: Example Walkthrough: The Leaky Tank
section_6.content: Apply the concept to a physics problem. A tank is leaking water at a rate defined by a function. We use the integral to find exactly how much total water was lost over 10 minutes.
section_6.example: Character: 'Rusty the Robot' is watching a water tank. The rate of flow is v(t) = 2t. By integrating, we find the volume V(t) = t², showing that after 10 minutes, 100 liters have leaked.

section_7.title: Summary: The Calculus Loop
section_7.content: Reinforce the 'Circular' nature of the relationship. Differentiation takes you from Accumulation to Rate; Integration takes you from Rate to Accumulation. End with a high-level visual summary.
section_7.example: Visual: An infinity-symbol shaped track. One side is labeled 'Derivatives (Rates)' and the other 'Integrals (Totals)'. A spark travels around the loop, connecting the two concepts forever.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed.
The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change.
This specific value is known as the derivative.
The total distance covered represents the accumulated change.
In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # --- Setup ---
        title = "The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah"
        lines = [
            "A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed.",
            "The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change.",
            "This specific value is known as the derivative.",
            "The total distance covered represents the accumulated change.",
            "In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Shared value tracker for time/progress
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Velocity function: v(t) = 0.2*t^2 + 1 (Smooth acceleration)
        def velocity_func(t):
            return 0.15 * t**2 + 1

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        # "A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Representing cheetah with a simple triangle and label
        cheetah_body = Triangle(color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/2).scale(0.2)
        cheetah_label = Text("Cheetah", font_size=16, color=ORANGE)
        cheetah = VGroup(cheetah_body, cheetah_label)
        cheetah_label.next_to(cheetah_body, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Path: Bottom grid row F1 to F6
        start_pos = self.grid["F1"]
        end_pos = self.grid["F6"]
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)

        self.play(FadeIn(cheetah))
        # Initial run to show the cheetah moving
        self.play(cheetah.animate.move_to(end_pos), run_time=3, rate_func=slow_into)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        # "The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.0,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(
            x_label=Text("Time", font_size=16), 
            y_label=Text("Speed", font_size=16)
        )
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        # Position graph in the upper/middle area
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "A1", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        curve = axes.plot(velocity_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels))
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        # "This specific value is known as the derivative."
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Reset time and cheetah for the synchronized demonstration
        time_tracker.set_value(0)
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)
        
        # Point on the graph curve
        dot_on_graph = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        dot_on_graph.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), velocity_func(time_tracker.get_value()))
        ))
        
        # Highlight on the y-axis
        h_line = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_horizontal_line(
            dot_on_graph.get_center(), color="#00FF00", stroke_width=2
        ))
        
        y_axis_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.06)
        y_axis_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            axes.c2p(0, velocity_func(time_tracker.get_value()))
        ))
        
        deriv_label = Text("Derivative (Speed)", font_size=14, color="#00FF00")
        # Position label relative to the y-axis point
        deriv_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(y_axis_dot, LEFT, buff=0.1))

        # Sync cheetah movement with the time tracker
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (time_tracker.get_value() / 4.0)
        ))

        self.add(dot_on_graph, h_line, y_axis_dot, deriv_label)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 4 ---
        # "The total distance covered represents the accumulated change."
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Shade the area under the curve
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 4], color="#FFFF00", opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 5 ---
        # "In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral."
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        integral_label = Text("Integral (Distance)", font_size=18, color="#FFFF00")
        # Place label inside or near the shaded area
        self.place_at_grid(integral_label, "C4")
        
        self.play(Write(integral_label))
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus bridges slope and area.",
            "It connects the derivative of a function to its integral.",
            "The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.",
            "Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.",
            "This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Dim all lecture lines initially
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_color(GRAY)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus bridges slope and area.
        # FTC formula \int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a) appears in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        formula = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # It connects the derivative of a function to its integral.
        # The screen splits into two panels: Panel A (left) and Panel B (right).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Panel A: f(x) = 2x
        ax_a = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 6], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5, 
                   axis_config={"include_tip": False}).set_color(GRAY)
        label_a = Text("Rate: f(x)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        panel_a = VGroup(ax_a, label_a)
        label_a.next_to(ax_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(panel_a, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Panel B: F(x) = x^2
        ax_b = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 9], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5,
                   axis_config={"include_tip": False}).set_color(GRAY)
        label_b = Text("Accumulation: F(x)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        panel_b = VGroup(ax_b, label_b)
        label_b.next_to(ax_b, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(panel_b, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(ax_a), Create(label_a), Create(ax_b), Create(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # Prepare for sync animations
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        
        f_curve = ax_a.plot(lambda x: 2*x, x_range=[0, 2.5], color=WHITE)
        F_curve = ax_b.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.5], color=WHITE)
        self.add(f_curve, F_curve)

        # Area under f(x) - persistent mobject
        area = VMobject(color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0)
        area.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners([
            ax_a.c2p(0, 0),
            *[ax_a.c2p(x, 2*x) for x in np.linspace(0, tracker.get_value(), 20)],
            ax_a.c2p(tracker.get_value(), 0),
            ax_a.c2p(0, 0)
        ]))

        # Point on F(x) - persistent mobject
        dot_b = Dot(color="#00BFFF")
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(ax_b.c2p(tracker.get_value(), tracker.get_value()**2)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.
        # Panel A shows area under f(x) filling up in #00FF00.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.add(area)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.
        # Panel B shows a point on the graph of F(x) rising in #00BFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.add(dot_b)
        self.play(Indicate(dot_b), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus.
        # A bridge icon in #FFD700 connects the panels as they animate in sync.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        bridge = DoubleArrow(
            start=ax_a.get_right(), 
            end=ax_b.get_left(), 
            color="#FFD700", 
            buff=0.1, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        bridge_label = Text("FTC BRIDGE", font_size=14, color="#FFD700").next_to(bridge, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        self.play(Create(bridge), Write(bridge_label))
        
        # Final sync movement
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        axes = Axes(

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_text = "Summary: The Calculus Loop"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Derivatives and integrals form a beautiful, continuous cycle.",
            "- Differentiation breaks a whole down into its parts.",
            "- Integration builds those parts back into a whole.",
            "- They are two sides of the same mathematical coin.",
            "- Master this connection to unlock the power of calculus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Derivatives and integrals form a beautiful, continuous cycle."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Infinity symbol (Lemniscate of Bernoulli)
        # x = a * cos(t) / (1 + sin^2(t)), y = a * sin(t) * cos(t) / (1 + sin^2(t))
        a_val = 1.8
        infinity_func = lambda t: np.array([
            a_val * np.cos(t) / (1 + (np.sin(t))**2),
            a_val * np.sin(t) * np.cos(t) / (1 + (np.sin(t))**2),
            0
        ])
        infinity_track = ParametricFunction(infinity_func, t_range=[0, TAU], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(infinity_track, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(infinity_track), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Differentiation breaks a whole down into its parts."
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        derivatives_label = Text("Derivatives\n(Rates)", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        # Positioning label near the left loop of the lemniscate
        self.place_at_grid(derivatives_label, 'C1', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(derivatives_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Integration builds those parts back into a whole."
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        integrals_label = Text("Integrals\n(Totals)", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        # Positioning label near the right loop of the lemniscate
        self.place_at_grid(integrals_label, 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(integrals_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "They are two sides of the same mathematical coin."
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Glowing spark travels around the track from left to right.
        # Proportion 0.5 is the leftmost point (t=PI). Proportion 1.0/0.0 is the rightmost point (t=0/TAU).
        spark_core = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.08)
        spark_glow = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.18, fill_opacity=0.3)
        spark = VGroup(spark_glow, spark_core)
        
        # Set spark at left loop (proportion 0.5)
        spark.move_to(infinity_track.point_from_proportion(0.5))
        self.add(spark)
        
        # Use ValueTracker for smooth continuous movement
        prop_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        spark.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(infinity_track.point_from_proportion(prop_tracker.get_value())))
        
        # Move from left (0.5) to right (1.0)
        self.play(prop_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Master this connection to unlock the power of calculus."
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Complete the circuit: travels from right back to left.
        # Seamlessly transition from 1.0 (end) to 0.0 (start) at the right tip.
        prop_tracker.set_value(0.0)
        # Move from right (0.0) back to left (0.5)
        self.play(prop_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        spark.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
outline.content: Introduce the concept of change versus accumulation using a Cheetah. A Cheetah's speedometer shows its 'Derivative' (velocity at an instant), while the total distance it covers represents the 'Integral' (accumulation over time). The goal is to show these aren't separate math topics, but two sides of the same coin.
outline.example: Visual: A Cheetah running across a savannah. An overlay shows a graph where the x-axis is time and the y-axis is speed. As the cheetah speeds up, the point on the graph moves higher.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed.
The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change.
This specific value is known as the derivative.
The total distance covered represents the accumulated change.
In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral.
animations: A cheetah [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] appears on the left and starts running across the screen.
A velocity-time graph appears above the cheetah with axes labeled in #FFFFFF.
A point moves along the graph's curve as the cheetah's speed varies.
The y-axis value is highlighted in #00FF00 and labeled 'Derivative (Speed)' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speed.svg].
The area under the curve is shaded in #FFFF00 and labeled 'Integral (Distance)'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # --- Setup ---
        title = "The Hook: The Speeding Cheetah"
        lines = [
            "A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed.",
            "The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change.",
            "This specific value is known as the derivative.",
            "The total distance covered represents the accumulated change.",
            "In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Shared value tracker for time/progress
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Velocity function: v(t) = 0.2*t^2 + 1 (Smooth acceleration)
        def velocity_func(t):
            return 0.15 * t**2 + 1

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        # "A cheetah sprints across the savannah at high speed."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Representing cheetah with a simple triangle and label
        cheetah_body = Triangle(color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/2).scale(0.2)
        cheetah_label = Text("Cheetah", font_size=16, color=ORANGE)
        cheetah = VGroup(cheetah_body, cheetah_label)
        cheetah_label.next_to(cheetah_body, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Path: Bottom grid row F1 to F6
        start_pos = self.grid["F1"]
        end_pos = self.grid["F6"]
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)

        self.play(FadeIn(cheetah))
        # Initial run to show the cheetah moving
        self.play(cheetah.animate.move_to(end_pos), run_time=3, rate_func=slow_into)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        # "The speedometer measures its instantaneous rate of change."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.0,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(
            x_label=Text("Time", font_size=16), 
            y_label=Text("Speed", font_size=16)
        )
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        # Position graph in the upper/middle area
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "A1", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        curve = axes.plot(velocity_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels))
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        # "This specific value is known as the derivative."
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Reset time and cheetah for the synchronized demonstration
        time_tracker.set_value(0)
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)
        
        # Point on the graph curve
        dot_on_graph = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        dot_on_graph.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), velocity_func(time_tracker.get_value()))
        ))
        
        # Highlight on the y-axis
        h_line = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_horizontal_line(
            dot_on_graph.get_center(), color="#00FF00", stroke_width=2
        ))
        
        y_axis_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.06)
        y_axis_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            axes.c2p(0, velocity_func(time_tracker.get_value()))
        ))
        
        deriv_label = Text("Derivative (Speed)", font_size=14, color="#00FF00")
        # Position label relative to the y-axis point
        deriv_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(y_axis_dot, LEFT, buff=0.1))

        # Sync cheetah movement with the time tracker
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (time_tracker.get_value() / 4.0)
        ))

        self.add(dot_on_graph, h_line, y_axis_dot, deriv_label)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 4 ---
        # "The total distance covered represents the accumulated change."
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Shade the area under the curve
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 4], color="#FFFF00", opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 5 ---
        # "In calculus, this total accumulation is called the integral."
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        integral_label = Text("Integral (Distance)", font_size=18, color="#FFFF00")
        # Place label inside or near the shaded area
        self.place_at_grid(integral_label, "C4")
        
        self.play(Write(integral_label))
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards
outline.content: Introduce the idea of 'Anti-differentiation.' If we have the velocity (the derivative), how do we find the total distance (the original function)? This sets the stage for the Integral as the 'undoing' of the Derivative.
outline.example: Visual: A 'Function Machine' where you drop in a function like x². The 'Derivative Lever' turns it into 2x. To get back to x², we need the 'Integral Lever'.

storyboard.title: The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards
lecture_lines: Integration is the inverse process of finding the derivative.
If we have velocity, we can recover total distance.
We call this process anti-differentiation or finding the integral.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards", 
            [
                "Integration is the inverse process of finding the derivative.",
                "If we have velocity, we can recover total distance.",
                "We call this process anti-differentiation or finding the integral."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors for consistency
        LINE1_COLOR = WHITE
        LINE2_COLOR = "#87CEEB" # Light blue
        LINE3_COLOR = "#90EE90" # Light green
        MACHINE_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LINE1_COLOR)
        
        # Create Function Machine
        machine_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, width=3.5, height=4, color=MACHINE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(machine_box, "B2", "E5")
        
        machine_label = Text("FUNCTION MACHINE", font_size=20, color=MACHINE_COLOR)
        # Position label manually relative to machine box to ensure it fits the visual style
        machine_label.move_to(machine_box.get_top() + DOWN * 0.4)
        
        # Levers
        derivative_lever = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*0.3, RIGHT*0.3, color=LINE2_COLOR),
            Circle(radius=0.1, color=LINE2_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        ).move_to(machine_box.get_right() + LEFT*0.3 + UP*0.5)
        
        derivative_text = Text("Derivative", font_size=16, color=LINE2_COLOR)
        derivative_text.next_to(derivative_lever, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        integral_lever = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*0.3, RIGHT*0.3, color=LINE3_COLOR),
            Circle(radius=0.1, color=LINE3_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        ).move_to(machine_box.get_right() + LEFT*0.3 + DOWN*0.5)
        
        integral_text = Text("Integral", font_size=16, color=LINE3_COLOR)
        integral_text.next_to(integral_lever, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Create(machine_box),
            Write(machine_label),
            FadeIn(derivative_lever),
            FadeIn(derivative_text),
            FadeIn(integral_lever),
            FadeIn(integral_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LINE2_COLOR)
        
        # x^2 enters
        input_x2 = MathTex("x^2", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(input_x2, "C1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(input_x2))
        self.play(input_x2.animate.move_to(machine_box.get_center()), run_time=1)
        
        # Lever pull animation
        self.play(
            derivative_lever.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.2),
            derivative_text.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.5
        )
        derivative_text.set_color(LINE2_COLOR)
        
        # 2x exits
        output_2x = MathTex("2x", color=LINE2_COLOR)
        output_2x.move_to(machine_box.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(input_x2, output_2x),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        end_pos_2x = self.grid["C6"]
        self.play(output_2x.animate.move_to(end_pos_2x), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE) # Keep visible but not highlighted
        self.lecture[2].set_color(LINE3_COLOR)
        
        # 2x enters back
        input_2x = MathTex("2x", color=LINE2_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(input_2x, "D1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(input_2x))
        self.play(input_2x.animate.move_to(machine_box.get_center()), run_time=1)
        
        # Integral lever pull
        self.play(
            integral_lever.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.2),
            integral_text.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.5
        )
        integral_text.set_color(LINE3_COLOR)
        
        # x^2 exits
        output_x2_final = MathTex("x^2", color=LINE3_COLOR)
        output_x2_final.move_to(machine_box.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(input_2x, output_x2_final),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        end_pos_x2 = self.grid["D6"]
        self.play(output_x2_final.animate.move_to(end_pos_x2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite Recap: The Slope of Change"
        lines = [
            "Differentiation helps us calculate the rate of change.",
            "Graphically, the derivative is the slope of the tangent.",
            "It transforms a position function into a velocity function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        POSITION_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Differentiation helps us calculate the rate of change."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Create axes for the graph
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE},
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Position-time curve (a hiker climbing)
        # f(x) = 0.2*x^2
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=POSITION_COLOR)
        
        # Labels for axes
        x_label = Text("Time (t)", font_size=16).next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        y_label = Text("Position (s)", font_size=16).rotate(90 * DEGREES).next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(x_label), Create(y_label))
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Graphically, the derivative is the slope of the tangent."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Tangent point at t=3
        t_val = 3.0
        point_on_curve = axes.c2p(t_val, 0.2 * t_val**2)
        dot = Dot(point_on_curve, color=WHITE)

outline.content: Present the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC). Explain that the area under a rate curve (f) can be found using its anti-derivative (F). This is the 'Aha!' moment where the slope and the area are mathematically linked.
outline.example: Mathematical Formula: ∫[a,b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Visual: Two screens side-by-side. Screen A shows the area filling up; Screen B shows a point moving up a position graph. They move in perfect synchronization.

lecture_lines: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus bridges slope and area.

The definite integral calculates net change over an interval.
Evaluation uses the anti-derivative at the boundary points.
This theorem unites the two main branches of calculus.

Panel A shows area under f(x) filling up in #00FF00.
Panel B shows a point on the graph of F(x) rising in #00BFFF.
A bridge icon in #FFD700 connects the panels as they animate in sync.

            "- Derivatives and integrals form a beautiful, continuous cycle.",

        infinity_func = lambda t: np.array([

            a_val * np.sin(t) * np.cos(t) / (1 + (np.sin(t))**2),

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Inverse Concept: Working Backwards", 
            [
                "Integration is the inverse process of finding the derivative.",
                "If we have velocity, we can recover total distance.",
                "We call this process anti-differentiation or finding the integral."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors for consistency
        LINE1_COLOR = WHITE
        LINE2_COLOR = "#87CEEB" # Light blue
        LINE3_COLOR = "#90EE90" # Light green
        MACHINE_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LINE1_COLOR)
        
        # Create Function Machine
        machine_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, width=3.5, height=4, color=MACHINE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.1)
        # Fix Issue 35: Moved machine_box from 'B2'-'E5' to 'B3'-'E6' to avoid crowding lecture text.
        self.place_in_area(machine_box, "B3", "E6")
        
        machine_label = Text("FUNCTION MACHINE", font_size=20, color=MACHINE_COLOR)
        machine_label.move_to(machine_box.get_top() + DOWN * 0.4)
        
        # Levers
        derivative_lever = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*0.3, RIGHT*0.3, color=LINE2_COLOR),
            Circle(radius=0.1, color=LINE2_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        ).move_to(machine_box.get_right() + LEFT*0.3 + UP*0.5)
        
        derivative_text = Text("Derivative", font_size=16, color=LINE2_COLOR)
        derivative_text.next_to(derivative_lever, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        integral_lever = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*0.3, RIGHT*0.3, color=LINE3_COLOR),
            Circle(radius=0.1, color=LINE3_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        ).move_to(machine_box.get_right() + LEFT*0.3 + DOWN*0.5)
        
        integral_text = Text("Integral", font_size=16, color=LINE3_COLOR)
        integral_text.next_to(integral_lever, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Create(machine_box),
            Write(machine_label),
            FadeIn(derivative_lever),
            FadeIn(derivative_text),
            FadeIn(integral_lever),
            FadeIn(integral_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LINE2_COLOR)
        
        # x^2 enters
        input_x2 = MathTex("x^2", color=WHITE)
        # Fix Issue 36: Moved input_x2 start position from 'C1' to 'C2' to avoid overlap with lecture text.
        self.place_at_grid(input_x2, "C2")

        self.play(input_x2.animate.move_to(machine_box.get_center()), run_time=1)
        
        # Lever pull animation
        self.play(
            derivative_lever.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.2),
            derivative_text.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.5
        )
        derivative_text.set_color(LINE2_COLOR)
        
        # 2x exits
        output_2x = MathTex("2x", color=LINE2_COLOR)
        output_2x.move_to(machine_box.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(input_x2, output_2x),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        end_pos_2x = self.grid["C6"]
        self.play(output_2x.animate.move_to(end_pos_2x), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(LINE3_COLOR)
        
        # 2x enters back
        input_2x = MathTex("2x", color=LINE2_COLOR)

        self.play(input_2x.animate.move_to(machine_box.get_center()), run_time=1)

            integral_text.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            rate_func=there_and_back,

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout and Titles
        self.setup_layout(
            "Example Walkthrough: The Leaky Tank",
            [
                "Consider a tank leaking water at a changing rate.",
                "Integrating the flow rate gives the total volume lost.",
                "Calculus provides exact answers for these real-world problems."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), run_time=1)

        # Load Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg]
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/water.svg]
        tank = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg", color=GREY_A)
        water = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/water.svg", color=BLUE_B)
        
        self.place_in_area(tank, "B1", "D3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_in_area(water, "B1", "D3", scale_factor=1.5)

        # ValueTracker for water level (0 to 1)
        water_level = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        # Capture initial water properties for scaling
        initial_water_height = water.height
        bottom_y = water.get_bottom()[1]

        def update_water(m):
            new_height = initial_water_height * water_level.get_value()
            if new_height > 0.01:
                m.stretch_to_fit_height(new_height)
                # Reposition bottom back to original bottom
                m.move_to([m.get_x(), bottom_y + new_height/2, 0])
            else:
                m.set_opacity(0)

        water.add_updater(update_water)

        self.play(FadeIn(tank), FadeIn(water), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(water_level.animate.set_value(0.3), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color Line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            run_time=1
        )

        # Plot rate function v(t) = 2t
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 2],
            y_range=[0, 20, 5],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        ).add_coordinates()
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)

        # v(t) = 2t plot
        v_graph = axes.plot(lambda t: 2*t, x_range=[0, 10], color="#FF4500")
        v_label = MathTex("v(t) = 2t", color="#FF4500")
        # Issue 46 Fix: func_label at A4 with scale 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A4", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Integral area
        area = axes.get_area(v_graph, x_range=[0, 10], color=BLUE_E, opacity=0.5)
        area_label = MathTex(r"V = \int_0^{10} 2t \, dt", color=BLUE_B)
        # Issue 45 Fix: area_label at A5 with scale 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(v_graph), Write(v_label), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(area), Write(area_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color Line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=1
        )

        # Result calculation
        result_tex = MathTex(r"= [t^2]_0^{10} = 100 \text{ L}", color=YELLOW)
        # Issue 44 Fix: result_tex at A6 with scale 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(result_tex, "A6", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Write(result_tex), run_time=2)
        self.wait(3)

        # Cleanup
        water.remove_updater(update_water)
